Alex (docs): Quick idea: add a tiny decision graphic to the error-ref entry that clarifies fallback order for 429s, timeouts, and context-limits. People keep asking which mechanism runs first.
Priya (eng-runtime): Strong +1. A compact chart or mermaid block should solve a lot of the confusion. We should call out streaming exceptions separately.
Dan (devex): I'll add a Mermaid draft in the PR. Minimal: ```mermaid
flowchart TD
  Req[Request] --> Err{Error type}
  Err -- 429 --> Retry[Client retry + backoff]
  Err -- timeout --> Trim[Trim / summarize + retry]
  Retry --> Throttled{Still throttled?}
  Throttled -- yes --> ModelDown[Model variant fallback]
  ModelDown --> Region[Region failover]
  Throttled -- no --> Success[OK]
```
Rina (eng-ml): Please annotate the diagram with triggers: 429 (rate), timeout (latency), queue-depth (backpressure). Also add a tiny note about KV cache compatibility when switching to quantized variants.
Alex (docs): I'll open a PR with the mermaid block + short prose and a small FAQ entry "When to retry vs trim?". Dan, can you add concise JS/Python snippets showing Retry-After handling and a backoff helper?
Dan (devex): Yep. JS snippet will parse Retry-After and use decorrelated jitter. Python will show a simple retry wrapper and mention circuit-breaker for persistent failures.
Priya (eng-runtime): I'll review the PR and add a test that simulates repeated 429s to verify our documented order. Docs-bot: PR opened by Alex: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/4521 :robot_face:
Alex (docs): Plan: merge after Dan's snippets and Priya signoff. Target EOD Thursday. Any objections?
Rina (eng-ml): No objections. I'll drop a tiny pseudo-snippet for trim-to-window behavior in the PR.
Alex (docs): Great, thanks everyone.
